speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent; could you tell me your age and how long you've noticed high blood pressure readings? Also, are you experiencing any headaches, dizziness, or changes in your vision?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the blood pressure was found incidentally during this well-child visit, could you tell me if the readings were taken in a calm setting or if the child was crying or anxious? Also, has anyone noticed any snoring, pauses in breathing during sleep, or excessive daytime sleepiness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify that blood pressure is typically measured in both arms and legs to check for consistency; could you tell me what the readings were in the left arm and both legs? Additionally, does your son have any symptoms like leg pain, weakness, or difficulty walking after activity?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to verify if there is a significant difference in blood pressure between the upper and lower extremities, so could you please provide the specific readings from his left arm and both legs? Additionally, have you noticed any weak pulses in his groin or feet, or does he seem to tire easily during play?

speaker: Patient
text: All systems review is essentially negative as reported by the mother.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the upper extremity hypertension suggests a possible obstruction, I need to confirm if there is a significant blood pressure gradient between his arms and legs. REQUEST TEST: Blood Pressure_arms_and_legs. Additionally, could you tell me if his femoral pulses feel weak or delayed compared to his radial pulses?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Pressure Differential: Upper Extremities 150/80 mm Hg (Right) with lower values in lower extremities, confirming a significant gradient. Pulses: 2+ radial pulses and trace femoral pulses, indicating weak and delayed femoral pulses compared to radial pulses.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood pressure gradient and weak femoral pulses are classic signs of coarctation of the aorta. To confirm the diagnosis and assess the severity, I will now order an echocardiogram. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram findings show narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a pressure gradient, consistent with coarctation of the aorta. Left ventricular function is normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: The echocardiogram confirms the narrowing of the aorta, so I am confident in the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the aorta.
